## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

# Worker Agents Skills

This repository bundles the baseline skills installed by [Worker
Agents](https://github.com/agents-dev/workerAgents).

The bundled skills are available under [`skills/`](skills/):

- `mcp-duckgo` — imported from `aahl/skills@mcp-duckgo`.

- `gauntlet-loop` — imported from `robonuggets/gauntlet-loop@gauntlet-loop`.
- `load-sketchfab-threejs` — local asset inspection, normalization, and Three.js/PlayCanvas A/B viewer skill.
- `opencode-zen-completions` — use the OpenCode Zen chat completions API for implementation work.

The original upstream licenses are preserved in
[`third-party-licenses/`](third-party-licenses/).

The repository is a clean scaffold, so I’m building this as a self-contained browser game: canvas-based visuals, keyboard and touch controls, five themed stages, four regular bosses, a final boss, and two timed bonus rounds.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, mobile-friendly 2D arcade street-fighting game in the existing repository.

## Requirements
- Five themed stages: school, streets, large shopping mall, broadcasting station construction site, and broadcaster’s hall.
- Two bonus stages, four normal bosses plus a final boss, each with a life bar.
- Include health, temporary invincibility, and extra-life power-ups.
- Support phone/tablet touch controls.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a self-contained HTML/CSS/Canvas game with original drawn graphics and no game framework.
- Used WASD/arrows, J (strike), K (power), and P (pause) on keyboard; added touch D-pad and action buttons.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the game UI and responsive styling in `index.html` and `style.css`.
- Implemented five stages, bosses, combat, pickups, bonus rounds, scoring, lives, pause, and end states in `game.js`.
- Ran `node --check game.js` successfully.
- Launched the local page in Playwright and captured desktop and mobile JPEG screenshots.

### Active
- No active changes; implementation is ready for further review.

### Blocked
- Browser check initially failed because Chromium was not installed; installed it and confirmed the page loads and starts.

## Next Move
1. Optionally inspect gameplay progression and touch controls in-browser, then fix any issues found.
2. Summarize the implementation and note assumptions to the user.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game canvas, HUD, title/pause overlays, and touch controls.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and responsive/mobile styling.
- `game.js`: Game logic, stage rendering, combat, bosses, bonus rounds, and controls.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Local preview was served with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- Screenshots saved to `/tmp/opencode/neon-riot.jpg`, `/tmp/opencode/neon-riot-play.jpg`, and `/tmp/opencode/neon-riot-mobile.jpg`.

Implemented **Neon Riot**, a playable, mobile-friendly arcade brawler in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.

It includes five themed stages, five boss fights with health bars, two timed bonus rounds, health/invincibility/extra-life pickups, scoring and combos, pause and restart, keyboard controls, and touch controls. The bonus rounds follow stages 2 and 4.

**Verified:** `node --check game.js` passes, and the game starts and pauses/resumes in-browser. Desktop and mobile layouts were also checked. Start a local server from the project directory with `python3 -m http.server 3002`, then open `http://localhost:3002`.
